title: My Love Is Like a Red, Red Rose
description: Robert Burns's love song, for 2 to 4 singers, sung to the tune "Low down in the Broom" as R. A. Smith printed it in The Scotish Minstrel. Two verses: the soprano sings the melody, and the alto, tenor and bass sing the words beneath it. Slow and tender.

credits.tune: traditional Scottish, "Low down in the Broom", as printed by R. A. Smith

licence.tune: public domain: traditional ("Low down in the Broom"), printed with these words by R. A. Smith (died 1829) in The Scotish Minstrel, vol. 3 (Edinburgh, undated, early 1820s)
licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella over R. A. Smith's piano chords (Smith died 1829); where the tune dips to middle C, the bass moves E, D, C under Smith's held C. Accepted exceptions (singable.py): the tune's own range as Smith prints it, which the licence keeps pitch for pitch: its dips to middle C, a tone under the beginner soprano range, on "love is", "a' the", "I will" and "'twere ten", where the alto sings the C with it over the tenor's G and the bass's E; and its high F and G, a semitone and a minor third over, on "love" ("So deep in love"), "weel", "And" and "will" ("And I will love thee still,"), with the alto on A, B and E under them.
licence.source: melody and words from The Scotish Minstrel, a selection from the vocal melodies of Scotland, ancient and modern, arranged for the piano forte by R. A. Smith (1780 to 1829), vol. 3 (Robert Purdie, Edinburgh; undated; archive.org dates this bound copy of vols. 1 to 3 to 1821), p. 85, "My Love Is Like a Red Red Rose", which the volume's index gives as Burns's words to the air "Low down in the Broom"; printed in C in common time and written here in C, every pitch as printed, the printed grace notes left out; the pickup kept as printed (a quaver and a semiquaver, three quarters of a beat), so the last "dry" is a quarter beat shorter than its printed dotted crotchet and the song ends on the bar line; verse 2 is the page's printed second verse, with "And the" and "While the" each sung on the printed quaver split into two semiquavers, and "Till" and "And" held over the tune's slurred notes as the page sets "And" in its last line; breaths written in for beginners: "June"/"sun", "I"/"while" and the second "dry"/"mile" (before "And") shortened by half a beat, "tune"/"run" by three quarters of a beat, the first "dry."/"mile." by a quarter beat (before the printed quaver rest), and verse 1's last "dry" by half a beat; the chords checked against Smith's piano bass; the melody checked against G. F. Graham, The Songs of Scotland, vol. 2 (Wood and Co., Edinburgh, 1848; some copies dated 1849), p. 28, arranged by T. M. Mudie; Burns died 1796, Smith 1829; read from the scans at archive.org/details/scotishminstrels00smit/page/n324 (the song) and /page/n237 (the index naming the air)
